questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am specifically passionate about the mexican Spanish and the mexican culture, which is why I chose that specific destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help from local friends I knew beforehand and from people from my host university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Find Facebook groups

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living in a closed neighborhood

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process was super long and complex since the mexican course catalog does not come out before it is too late to register/get approval in Denmark. Besides this, both the Danish and the Mexican university were very slow in replying on mail. Also in my case, my courses got accepted by the Danish university but then in the last moment not, which was a very stressful situation. I hope this does not happen to other students in the future.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very simple. You would just talk with the person in charge of the international students and they would fix it for you. Only thing you have to do is make sure there is space in the course and that the ours fit to your schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people in charge of the international students were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful, not until the end at least.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk a lot about it with your home institution before, and explain that the course catalog in the case of México does not come out before very late.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything is very different. A completely different system regarding teaching, grading and attendance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- contemporary Latin America 
- pre Hispanic arts of the north of México 
-  language and computers 
- globalization and communication 
- temas selectos 3 (linguist justice)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you study and what you want to study. But my host institution has every kind of course so there are options of everything you could imagine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different kinda of social and cultural events, sports area free for everyone and activities that teaches you about political issues of the country

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Look for the more mexican things/people rather than just going to the places where the international students go.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible to the states close by.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open minded and don’t be scared to be social/talk. People are friendly and will receive you with joy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, it is not my first time here so I was already used to the cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The school system is completely different, so be prepared for that
2. This destination is quite safe, but you should still be aware and careful of where you go 
3. It is the most beautiful campus with very good courses and teachers

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open minded, say yes to things/opportunities, engage with the locals and the culture

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know more of the mexican culture, making more contacts and bettering my Spanish

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic level of the university as well as taking my Spanish to the next level

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
